newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON WINS AAU SULLIVAN AWARD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON WINS AAU SULLIVAN AWARD.

text.p: Double Olympic gold medalist Michael Johnson was named recipient of the 1996 James E. Sullivan Memorial Award, the Amateur Athletic Union announced Friday.
Johnson received the honour, presented each year by the AAU to America's top amateur athlete, for his historic exploits at the Atlanta Olympics.
Johnson last summer became the first man to win gold medals in the 200 and 400 meters at the same Olympics, recording an astounding world record time of 19.32 seconds in the 200 meters.
"It is a great honour to receive the 1996 AAU Sullivan Award," Johnson said in a release issued by the AAU. "1996 was indeed a career year for me in winning two Olympic gold medals.
"Winning this award is a great acknowledgment of these achievements," Johnson said.

Johnson became the 37th track and field athlete to win the Sullivan Award, which completed a hat trick of such honours for the Dallas native. Johnson also received the Jesse Owens Award and was named the United States Olympic Committee's Man of the Year for 1996.

The other finalists for the 67th annual Sullivan Award were golf sensation Tiger Woods, who won his third U.S. Amateur crown before turning pro last year, Olympic 100 meters champion Gail Devers, figure skating world champion Michele Kwan, Olympic decathlon gold medalist Dan O'Brien, quadruple Olympic gold medal swimmer Amy Van Dyken, women's softball star Dot Richarson, women's basketball standout Teresa Edwards, gymnast Shannon Miller and star college quarterback Danny Wuerffel.
